en.question: Which signal in production most directly indicates that a prompt change has degraded quality, as opposed to an infrastructure problem?

options.text: A rise in p99 latency on the endpoint that serves the feature.
options.note: Latency is an infrastructure symptom and says nothing about correctness.

options.text: An increase in HTTP 429 responses returned by the Claude API.
options.note: 429s indicate rate limiting, which is unrelated to prompt content.

options.text: A drop in the eval score and a rise in user corrections after the change.
A rise in the average number of input tokens per request.
options.note: Token growth affects cost and may follow a longer prompt without harming quality.

en.explanation: Quality regressions show up in quality measurements. The eval score is the controlled signal and user corrections are the field signal; together they point at content rather than infrastructure.
